note: First draft, written from knowledge.json. Edit freely: the ads brief shows whatever is here. Every line must be something a real person can say or film. A number is only allowed if it is in knowledge.json or read off the screen during the shoot. Lines in [square brackets] are prompts for the person on camera, not a script.

ideas.title: The ball tells the truth
ideas.who: One real customer hitting, a fitter talking

hook.say: The swing may lie, but the ball tells the truth.
hook.show: A ball leaving the club face in a TrackMan bay, then the numbers coming up on the screen.

points: This is their own club. These are the numbers.
One change: a shaft that suits the swing. Same golfer, same day.
The ball speaks. Data confirms. Feel seals the deal.
shots: Side-on swing with their own club, then the screen
The fitter swapping the shaft
The same swing again, then the screen
The golfer's face on the second set of numbers
ideas.watch_out: Use the real numbers from the session. If the difference is small, say so. Never a made-up number.

ideas.title: When last did anyone measure your swing?
ideas.who: A fitter to camera, a golfer on the bay behind them

hook.say: When last did anyone measure your swing?
hook.show: A golfer mid-swing on the bay. The numbers appear on the screen behind the fitter.

points: You hit your own clubs on TrackMan first, so we see where you are.
Then we change one thing at a time and watch what the ball does.
ClubLab builds the result: loft, lie, length, swing weight, shaft and grip, matched to your spec.
shots: The golfer's swing, side on
The TrackMan screen with the real numbers
The fitter handing over a different club
A finished club on the ClubLab bench
ideas.watch_out: Never talk down. The golfer in the shot should look like they are enjoying it.

ideas.title: Three feels, not thirty
ideas.who: The coach to camera, on the bay

hook.say: You will leave your lesson with three things to feel. Not thirty.
hook.show: The coach close to camera on the bay, holding up three fingers.

points: Every session is limited to three key feels, so you remember them on the course.
You see your swing on video and your numbers on TrackMan.
You get both after the lesson, to practise with.
shots: Coach to camera, eye level
Coach and student looking at the swing video together
The student hitting one more, coach nodding
ideas.watch_out: The coach says it their own way. The three feels are the promise, keep that line.

ideas.title: Show me your normal swing
ideas.who: The coach with a real student

hook.say: Show me your normal swing. Don't fix anything.
hook.show: The coach standing beside a student at address. The student swings.

points: [Coach: watch one swing, then name the one thing that matters most.]
[Student hits again. Show what the ball does on the screen, whatever it is.]
[Coach to camera: who you are and when you coach at Swing Shack.]
shots: Wide: coach and student on the bay
The first swing, side on
Coach's hands showing the one change
The second swing and the screen
ideas.watch_out: A real lesson moment, not acted. If the second swing is not better, film another student.

ideas.title: Where does the putt start?
ideas.who: A fitter and a real customer with their own putter

hook.show: Low camera behind the ball. A customer strokes a putt with their own putter.

points: [Fitter: the first thing you check when you fit a putter, in your own words.]
[The same putt with a putter that suits them. Show what changed.]
[Customer: what felt different.]
shots: Low behind the ball, their own putter
Close on the putter face at address
The same angle with the fitted putter
The customer's reaction
ideas.watch_out: Show what really happened. No claims about how many putts it saves.

ideas.title: Your first visit
ideas.who: A host walking the viewer in

hook.say: Never been to an indoor golf club? Here is what your first visit looks like.
hook.show: The camera walks in at Old Parktonian Sports Club and a host turns to greet it.

points: Four TrackMan bays, including TrackMan iO.
Play any of more than 400 courses, or just practise.
Someone sets you up and stays close if you want help.
shots: Walking in through the door
The bays, wide
A course loading on the screen
A host setting up a bay for a new visitor
ideas.watch_out: It should feel like being welcomed, not like a tour of equipment.

ideas.title: What members get
ideas.who: A real member, or a host beside one

hook.say: Here is what a Swing Shack membership actually gets you.
hook.show: A member walking to their bay with their bag over a shoulder.

points: Four free practice sessions every month.
25% off fittings.
15% off lessons.
shots: Member arriving, bag on shoulder
Member mid-practice on the bay
Each benefit as on-screen text while they hit
Member and host talking after the session
ideas.watch_out: Only these three benefits, exactly as written. End on: Join the club.

ideas.title: In their words
ideas.who: A real customer, filmed straight after their session

hook.say: [Customer, to camera:] I did not expect that.
hook.show: The customer on the bay, club still in hand, the screen behind them.

points: [What did you come in for, and what did you expect?]
[What surprised you?]
[What would you tell a friend who is thinking about it?]
shots: Customer to camera, chest up, bay behind them
A cutaway to one of their swings
A cutaway to the screen
ideas.watch_out: Their words, not a script. If they say a number it must be the one that was on the screen.

ideas.title: The product moves by itself
ideas.who: Nobody. The product is the character

hook.say: No voice. Music or bay sound only.
hook.show: A still of the product that moves as if someone is using it: the bag stands itself up, the glove flexes, the ball rolls out of the sleeve.
hook.text: The product name, then where to get it.

points: One movement, start to finish. Not three.
The product stays sharp and true to colour the whole time.
End on the still product and the brand name.
shots: One clean product photo on a plain or in-store background
The same photo with room around it for the movement
ideas.watch_out: Retail only. It has to move; a flat photo is not an ad.
